Jwt.//Key: Supplied at runtime via the Jwt__Key environment variable. Never commit a signing key here.
Jwt.//ExpiresInSeconds: Access token lifetime, 2 hours. The client keeps it in a script-readable cookie, so this is the window an XSS-stolen token stays usable; the 7-day refresh cookie mints replacements silently, which is what lets it be shortened again without anyone noticing.

BackgroundJobs.//Capacity: Maximum jobs waiting to be picked up. Bounded on purpose — an unbounded queue turns a request burst into unbounded memory growth and an OOM that names nothing. At the limit, enqueue applies backpressure instead of dropping work.
BackgroundJobs.//ShutdownGrace: How long a job already running is given to finish once shutdown starts, before its token is signalled. HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout is derived from this plus a margin, so the host never kills the process while a job is still inside its grace window.

ServiceBus.//ConnectionString: Empty disables messaging entirely, so the API still runs with no broker present. Supplied at runtime via ServiceBus__ConnectionString — the emulator's development string locally, a Container Apps secret in Azure. Never committed.
ServiceBus.//MaxConcurrentCalls: Messages handled at once by ONE consumer.
ServiceBus.//ConsumersPerSubscription: Independent processors per subscription. In production these are replicas; more than one in a single process is what lets a laptop show competing consumers do not double-process.
ServiceBus.//MaxDeliveryCount: Mirrors the broker's own setting, for log messages only. The real limit lives on the subscription (Azure, or the emulator's Config.json) and no client setting can override it.
